To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
F. novi-cida replicates within vacuoles within H. vermifor-mis and the iglC locus of the Francisella pathogenic island is essential for this process.

Francisella novicida survives, proliferates and replicates within Hartmannella vermifomis, and that the Francisella pathogenic island locus igl is required for the intracellular proliferation of the bacteria within H. vermifomis.
F. noviicida survives and proliferates in vacuoles within H. vermifornis cells, which are different from the acidic vacuoles in which it resides in mammalian cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the intracellular replication of a facultative intracellular pathogen, F. novocida, within a free-living environmental ameba, H. vermiformi.
the survival and proliferation of F. tularemia in the environment.
the intracellular lifestyle of the bacterium F. tulareis in free-living amebas and its potential as a biological reservoir in water resources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
F. tularenisis is a facultative intracellular bacterial pathogen of amebae.
F. tularesis has an intra-vacuole replication strategy within H. vermifomis and does not escape from the vacuole into the cytosolic compartment of the ameba cells.
F. novocida does not replicate within H. vermifomis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
F. novocida does not replicate within the acidified phagolysosomes of H. vermifromis.
Francisella pathogenic island locus igl C gene product is required for intracellular proliferation of Francisella novicida within Hartmannella vermifomis.
F. noviicida does not escape from the vacuoles in H. vermifomis and replicates in vacuole.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Francisella is able to survive within H. vermifromis, but does not replicate.
Francisella is not a pathogen of free-living amoebae.
F. novocida replicates within vacuoles within amoebae, and this replication is dependent upon IglC.
